methods.label: Bound the smallest altitude
methods.sourceMethod: Uses the reciprocal-altitude identity supplied by LIVE and AoPS Solution 1, together with the strict triangle inequality to obtain 2r<a<=3r. Completes the integer cases explicitly, including both possible values of b when r=2 and a=5.

annotationRationale: The central steps connect altitudes to the inradius through area, then use triangle feasibility and integrality to exhaust the possibilities. The references share this underlying route, so their equivalent casework is consolidated into one method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The statement, choices, and key agree. Independently, the only feasible triples are (3,3,3), (6,6,6), and (9,9,9), giving 3, choice B. There are no figures or grading contradictions.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. LIVE's enumeration and AoPS Solution 1 use the same reciprocal-altitude identity and integer casework; consolidating them into the stronger smallest-altitude bound is appropriate. Another enumeration would add little.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed area-inradius and integer-equation concepts describe the central reasoning. Triangle area and triangle inequality are appropriate support concepts; no contextual additions are needed.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The area decompositions correctly give \(1/r=1/a+1/b+1/c\). The altitude cap gives \(r\le3\), and strict triangle inequality gives \(2r<a\le3r\). For r=1 this forces (3,3,3). For r=2, a=6 forces (6,6,6), while a=5 permits only b=5 or 6, producing c=10 or 15/2. For r=3, the reciprocal lower bounds force (9,9,9). Equilateral triangles with these altitudes establish existence and integer inradius.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The method correctly credits LIVE and AoPS as nonofficial sources and uses source-informed-original. Its prose independently explains their common route. The explicit b=5,6 check supplies the completeness missing from AoPS's abbreviated a=5 discussion.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why reciprocal side lengths help. The inradius formula is derived at use, strictness excludes degeneracy, all integer cases are shown, and the final construction proves realizability.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four direct IDs are supported: triangle-area-radius relations supplies K=rs, integer-diophantine-equations covers the complete bounded integer search, cnm_111 supplies strict triangle inequality, and cnm_p148 supplies base-height area.

nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 6.G.A.1 link supports triangle area, and the partial 7.G.A.2 link supports triangle feasibility without claiming construction coverage. Neither link covers the central inradius and integer-equation synthesis.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct concepts and question-level assessed/support roles fit the written argument. The reciprocal-altitude identity is fully derived and needs no additional catalog node.
